paragraphs: Multi-instance point cloud registration means finding the position and orientation of every occurrence of a reference object in a three-dimensional scene. Clutter and occlusion make this difficult: points belonging to different objects can become hard to distinguish. Existing approaches first establish matches across the whole scene and then group those matches into individual instances.

This paper changes the sequence by locating candidate objects before matching their points. A focusing module uses self-attention and cross-attention to relate the reference point cloud to structurally similar objects. It predicts object centers and produces candidate regions. A second module then estimates a separate pose for each candidate, turning the overall problem into multiple pairwise registration problems.

The matching module uses both an instance mask and an overlap mask to improve point correspondences. These address which points belong to the candidate instance and which participate in the shared region. Experiments on Scan2CAD and ROBI report state-of-the-art results, supporting the effectiveness of focusing on individual objects before detailed matching.
neurips-2024-3d-focusing-and-matching-ne.tldr: A two-stage network locates candidate objects before matching their points, improving multi-instance 3D pose estimation on two benchmarks.

paragraphs: Knowledge distillation trains a smaller student language model with guidance from a larger teacher, aiming to retain useful capabilities while reducing computation and memory requirements. Common approaches make the student's predicted probabilities resemble the teacher's probabilities directly. This paper investigates a different training target, drawing on imitation learning to describe the gap between their behaviors.

The method matches action-value moments: statistical quantities associated with the value of the teacher's actions. It considers these quantities from both on-policy and off-policy perspectives, incorporating different relationships between the behavior being evaluated and the policy producing it. An adversarial training procedure jointly estimates the moment-matching distance and adjusts the student to reduce that distance.

This makes the measure of imitation part of the learning process, rather than relying solely on an explicit divergence between output probabilities. Experiments cover general instruction following and task-specific settings, where the authors report new state-of-the-art performance. Those results support moment matching as an effective distillation objective across the evaluated settings.
neurips-2024-adversarial-moment-matching.tldr: Adversarial moment matching trains smaller language models to imitate a teacher's behavior and achieves leading results in the reported distillation experiments.

paragraphs: Distributed computation can be disrupted when some workers are slow or return unreliable results. Coded computing addresses this by giving workers combinations of data and decoding their collective outputs. This paper develops a learning-theoretic foundation intended to make that approach better suited to machine learning workloads, with reconstruction accuracy as the central objective.

The framework chooses encoding and decoding functions to minimize mean squared error between the recovered and true results. Its analysis bounds that error using two contributions: the decoder's generalization error and the encoder's training error. Within a second-order Sobolev function space, the authors derive optimal encoder and decoder functions, connecting the design problem to a specified mathematical setting.

For N workers and at most S stragglers, the proposed solution has error rates O(S³N⁻³) without computation noise and O(S^(8/5)N^(-3/5)) with noise. These rates describe how worker count and straggler count affect accuracy in the analyzed settings. Machine learning inference experiments also report better accuracy and convergence rates than existing state-of-the-art methods.
neurips-2024-coded-computing-for-resilie.tldr: A learning-theoretic coded computing framework designs encoders and decoders with provable error rates and improved machine learning inference results.

paragraphs: Compiler backends translate programs into machine code for particular processors. Supporting many processor designs requires specialized backend development, which the paper describes as laborious and difficult to automate. Although language models can assist with programming, suitable training data has been a barrier to applying them to this specialized work.

ComBack provides a public dataset covering 178 backends from mainstream compilers. It organizes development assistance into three tasks: completing statements, suggesting the next statement, and generating code. These tasks connect the dataset to common editing and implementation activities. Fine-tuning experiments with six pretrained language models show improved accuracy across all three tasks.

The authors also evaluate their strongest model, CodeT5+, on new targets. With 220 million parameters after ComBack fine-tuning, it substantially outperforms Fork-Flow methods and surpasses ChatGPT-3.5-Turbo and Code-LLaMA-34B-Instruct in the reported comparisons. These findings show the value of specialized training data for backend assistance and suggest potential development-efficiency gains; the stated measurements concern task accuracy.
neurips-2024-comback-a-versatile-dataset.tldr: ComBack supplies compiler-backend training tasks that improve code-model accuracy and help a fine-tuned CodeT5+ outperform the reported alternatives.

paragraphs: Machine learning models are commonly tested by measuring overall performance on held-out data or examining selected subgroups. The paper argues that this treats available data as the sole guide to testing, leaving useful contextual information outside the process. Its proposed alternative, Context-Aware Testing, uses context to guide the search toward meaningful model failures.

The authors implement this idea in SMART Testing. A large language model proposes failures that appear relevant and likely given the context. These hypotheses are then assessed against data through a self-falsification mechanism. The resulting workflow combines context-driven hypothesis generation with empirical checking, so a plausible account of a failure is a starting point for evaluation.

Across diverse empirical settings, SMART identifies failures that the authors find more relevant and impactful than those found by alternatives. The contribution is therefore a way to direct testing effort as well as a concrete testing system. The results support using contextual knowledge to shape what gets investigated while retaining data as the means of evaluating proposed failures.
neurips-2024-context-aware-testing-a-new.tldr: SMART Testing uses contextual knowledge and language-model hypotheses to find empirically checked model failures that are more relevant and impactful in the reported evaluations.

paragraphs: Sharing data for machine learning can expose sensitive information alongside useful attributes. Decoupling methods try to separate those two kinds of information so that released representations or synthetic data remain useful while reducing privacy concerns. This paper addresses how to compare such methods systematically when the release is not tailored to one particular downstream task.

DECO-Bench brings decoupling techniques, synthetic data generation, and evaluation protocols into a unified framework. That shared structure makes the relationship between privacy and utility the central comparison. A method must be assessed for how well it separates sensitive information and for how much useful information remains available after the transformation.

The authors use the framework to benchmark multiple techniques and examine their privacy-utility trade-offs. They also release source code, pretrained models, and datasets of decoupled representations to support further research. The main contribution is an organized basis for evaluating methods together, addressing the stated absence of a standard benchmark for task-agnostic decoupling.
neurips-2024-deco-bench-unified-benchmar.tldr: DECO-Bench unifies methods and evaluation protocols for comparing privacy-utility trade-offs in task-agnostic synthetic data release.

paragraphs: Gaussian splatting represents a three-dimensional scene with a collection of Gaussian distributions and uses that representation to produce images from new viewpoints. The paper identifies a difficulty with this design: smooth, continuous distributions do not accurately represent the abrupt image changes found at discontinuities and boundaries. Those sharp transitions are the focus of the proposed method.

DisC-GS introduces a framework for making Gaussian splatting aware of discontinuities during rendering. This raises a related optimization issue, because the proposed rendering process must still provide useful gradients for learning. The authors address it with a Bézier-boundary gradient approximation, designed to retain differentiability in an approximate form while accommodating the boundary-aware rendering process.

The contribution connects two requirements: representing abrupt visual changes and preserving a way to optimize the scene representation through gradients. The authors report extensive experiments demonstrating the framework's effectiveness. Their stated result supports the proposed treatment of discontinuities, with the methodological emphasis on how boundary handling and gradient-based optimization can work together.
neurips-2024-disc-gs-discontinuity-aware.tldr: DisC-GS adds discontinuity-aware rendering to Gaussian splatting and approximates boundary gradients to keep the process trainable.

paragraphs: Combinatorial optimization searches among discrete choices for a solution with the best objective value. The paper focuses on a search difficulty: at each iteration, existing methods can inspect only a small fraction of the possible solutions. Information from distant parts of that space may therefore be difficult for the solver to use when choosing its next move.

The proposed framework applies heat diffusion to the target function while preserving its optima. Diffusion lets information from distant regions influence the function encountered by the solver. This changes the guidance available during search without changing which solutions are optimal. The central idea is to improve the information reaching the solver through a transformed objective.

The authors present the approach as a framework for general combinatorial optimization and report superior performance across a range of challenging problems. These findings support heat diffusion as a useful mechanism for navigating discrete solution spaces. The paper also connects this result to the broader potential of thermodynamic ideas in computational methods, specifically their use for optimization.
neurips-2024-efficient-combinatorial-opt.tldr: An optima-preserving heat-diffusion transformation helps combinatorial solvers use information from distant solutions and improves performance in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: In multi-label learning, an example can have several labels, and the space of possible combinations can be large and sparse. Active learning adds a resource constraint: the model must choose which examples are most useful to label. Evidential Mixture Machines address both prediction and selection by modeling relationships among labels together with uncertainty.

The method builds on mixtures of Bernoulli components, which represent correlated label patterns through a smaller space of mixture weights. Components are learned without supervision in the label space, while evidential learning connects input features to uncertain predictions of their weights. The predicted coefficients are also combined into proxy pseudo counts to improve component offset predictions.

For selecting examples, EMM combines evidential uncertainty with predicted covariances in label embeddings. This gives the selection rule information about both uncertainty and label relationships. Synthetic experiments support its uncertainty estimates and ability to capture correlations. Evaluations on real-world datasets report improved performance over existing multi-label active learning methods, supporting the combined prediction-and-selection design.
neurips-2024-evidential-mixture-machines.tldr: Evidential Mixture Machines combine label correlations and uncertainty estimates to improve multi-label prediction and active sample selection.

paragraphs: Invisible image watermarks embed a hidden message while aiming to preserve the visible image. They can support content authentication and copyright protection, but the paper identifies regeneration attacks as a weakness of existing methods. FreqMark targets this robustness problem through the space in which it optimizes the watermark.

The method first encodes an image with a variational autoencoder, or VAE. It then performs unconstrained optimization in the frequency space of that latent representation to embed the message. A pretrained image encoder extracts the watermark. This formulation provides a flexible trade-off between visible image quality and how well the hidden information survives attacks, along with a choice of message length.

The authors report advantages in both image quality and robustness, including resistance to regeneration attacks. For a 48-bit hidden message, bit accuracy exceeds 90% under the evaluated attack scenarios. This measures how accurately individual message bits are recovered in those experiments, supporting the approach's robustness without asserting perfect recovery of every complete message.
neurips-2024-freqmark-invisible-image-wa.tldr: FreqMark optimizes latent image frequencies to embed robust invisible watermarks, exceeding 90% bit accuracy for 48-bit messages in the reported attack scenarios.

paragraphs: Particle-based variational inference represents a target distribution using particles that move according to a gradient flow. Recent methods use expressive function spaces, including neural networks, to model that motion. The paper addresses a gap in these methods: they are mainly designed for unconstrained domains, although sampling may require every particle to remain inside a specified region.

The proposed constrained functional gradient flow, or CFG, introduces a boundary condition that confines particles to the allowed domain. This makes the constraint part of the flow itself. The domain boundary also produces a boundary integral term, and the authors develop numerical strategies for handling that term when implementing the method.

The theoretical result establishes convergence in total variation for the continuous-time formulation. That qualification matters because the guarantee is stated for the underlying flow. Experiments also demonstrate the framework's effectiveness. Together, the boundary condition, numerical treatment, and convergence analysis provide a framework for extending functional-gradient particle methods to constrained sampling problems.
neurips-2024-functional-gradient-flows-f.tldr: CFG introduces boundary-aware particle flows for constrained sampling, with continuous-time convergence guarantees and numerical methods for boundary terms.

paragraphs: Few-shot learning depends heavily on prior knowledge because each new task provides little data. Meta-learning gathers that knowledge across related tasks, but commonly uses a prespecified probability distribution, such as a Gaussian, to express it. The paper argues that a restricted prior shape can limit performance when examples are especially scarce.

The proposed method learns the prior from the available tasks using a non-injective change-of-variables model, called NCoV. A non-injective transformation can map multiple inputs to the same output. Here, that flexibility supports modeling a broad range of probability densities. The authors argue that NCoV is more expressive than conventional change-of-variables models, particularly in high-dimensional settings.

A theoretical analysis establishes a universal approximation capacity for the model. Experiments on three few-shot learning datasets show advantages for learned priors over prespecified ones, with pronounced benefits under extremely limited data. These results connect distributional flexibility to practical adaptation: a prior fitted to related tasks can supply more useful guidance when a new task offers few observations.
neurips-2024-meta-learning-universal-pri.tldr: NCoV learns expressive priors from related tasks, with universal approximation theory and improved few-shot results when data is especially scarce.

paragraphs: Cooperative learning often assumes that one learning system controls every agent, or that it controls just one agent working with unfamiliar teammates. Many settings fall between these cases. A group trained together may need to cooperate with other groups, while the number and behavior of teammates change. This paper formalizes that broader situation as N-agent ad hoc teamwork.

The authors propose Policy Optimization with Agent Modelling, or POAM, to address the problem. It is a policy-gradient approach to multi-agent reinforcement learning that learns representations of teammate behavior. Those representations support adaptation to diverse teammates, making the behavior of other agents an explicit part of learning how to cooperate.

Evaluations use tasks from the multi-agent particle environment and StarCraft II. POAM improves cooperative returns relative to the tested baselines and generalizes to unseen teammates outside the training distribution. These findings support both the usefulness of the broader problem formulation and the value of learning teammate representations for cooperation under changing team composition.
neurips-2024-n-agent-ad-hoc-teamwork-84c.tldr: POAM learns teammate-behavior representations to improve cooperation when the number and types of teammates vary.

paragraphs: Predicting what a robot will see next and deciding how it should move both depend on the dynamics of the same physical situation. Diffusion models have been used for image generation and for generating robot actions through denoising. PAD brings these capabilities into a joint process so that future visual observations and actions are predicted together.

The framework uses Diffusion Transformers to integrate images and robot states within the shared denoising process. It supports co-training on robotic demonstrations and large video datasets, connecting policy learning with visual prediction data. The authors also describe extending the approach to additional robotic modalities, including depth images.

On the full Metaworld benchmark, a single text-conditioned visual policy achieves a reported 38.9% relative improvement in a data-efficient imitation-learning setting. Real-world manipulation experiments also show better generalization to unseen tasks, with a reported 28.0% increase in success rate over the strongest baseline. These findings support the usefulness of learning prediction and action together in the evaluated robotic settings.
neurips-2024-prediction-with-action-visu.tldr: PAD jointly denoises future images and robot actions, improving benchmark performance and generalization to unseen real-world manipulation tasks.

paragraphs: Answering a question about an image requires extracting visual information and reasoning with it. Vision-language models usually intertwine these abilities, making their separate contributions difficult to assess. Prism introduces a two-stage framework that makes the division explicit, providing a way to compare perception and reasoning capabilities across proprietary and open-source models.

In the first stage, a vision-language model converts relevant visual information into text. In the second, a language model uses that textual description to answer the question. This creates a clear interface between seeing and reasoning. It also allows a streamlined visual model to be paired with a stronger language model for the reasoning stage.

The authors report that this combination can improve general vision-language performance while substantially reducing training and operating expenses. On MMStar, a configuration using a vanilla 2B LLaVA model and GPT-3.5 matches the performance of vision-language models ten times larger. The result supports Prism's potential as both an assessment framework and a cost-effective approach to visual question solving.
neurips-2024-prism-a-framework-for-decou.tldr: Prism separates visual perception from language-based reasoning, enabling capability comparisons and competitive visual-question performance with a smaller visual model.

paragraphs: Online learning makes predictions or decisions sequentially as information arrives. Performance is measured through regret, which captures accumulated loss relative to a comparison choice. This paper studies how to obtain low regret while providing differential privacy, focusing on prediction from experts and online convex optimization. Its main tool is a transformation of lazy algorithms, which switch decisions infrequently.

Applying this transformation to existing algorithms gives private methods with improved regret when the privacy parameter epsilon is much smaller than one. The reported bounds are sqrt(T log d) + T^(1/3) log(d)/epsilon^(2/3) for prediction from experts and sqrt(T) + T^(1/3) sqrt(d)/epsilon^(2/3) for convex optimization. These expressions quantify the privacy-related contribution alongside the other regret term.

The paper also proves a lower bound for private prediction from experts. It establishes optimality within a natural family of private algorithms that switch infrequently. This scope is central to the result: the optimality statement applies to that low-switching family. Together, the transformation and bound clarify the usefulness of laziness for private sequential learning.
neurips-2024-private-online-learning-via.tldr: A transformation of low-switching online algorithms improves regret under strong privacy and achieves family-specific optimality for prediction from experts.

paragraphs: Diffusion models can fill missing data, but the paper identifies two tensions with using them directly. Their emphasis on producing diverse samples can work against accurate recovery of missing values. Training with data masking also reduces the entries available for learning. NewImp addresses both issues by reformulating imputation through a Wasserstein gradient-flow perspective.

The first change adds negative-entropy regularization to the cost functional. This term suppresses diversity to improve imputation accuracy, aligning the objective with the recovery task. The second change concerns how the imputation procedure is expressed: the authors show that the procedure induced by a conditional-distribution cost can equivalently be replaced by one induced by the joint distribution.

That equivalence removes the need for data masking within the proposed formulation. The two changes therefore address separate obstacles: the diversity encouraged by the objective and the observable information used during training. Extensive experiments support the method's effectiveness, showing the practical value of adapting diffusion-based learning to the particular requirements of missing-data inference.
neurips-2024-rethinking-the-diffusion-mo.tldr: NewImp adapts diffusion-based imputation by suppressing sample diversity and using a joint-distribution formulation that eliminates training-time data masking.

paragraphs: Automated sleep staging can combine physiological signals such as EEG, EOG, and EMG, but some modalities may be unavailable in practice. Missing inputs can undermine models trained to use them together. CIMSleepNet addresses this problem while also modeling temporal context, so its design considers both interactions among signal types and information across time.

A modality-awareness imagination module learns a shared representation distribution to capture relationships among modalities. A contrastive calibration component uses semantic and modality information to check consistency while preserving what is distinctive about each signal type. This calibration aligns the distribution recovered by the imagination module with the real data distribution.

The framework also uses multi-level cross-branch temporal attention to capture interactions within individual epochs and between epochs. These components connect missing-modality recovery with the temporal structure needed for sleep staging. Experiments on five multimodal sleep datasets report substantial gains over competitive methods under various missing-modality patterns, supporting the framework's robustness across the evaluated patterns of incomplete signals.
neurips-2024-robust-sleep-staging-over-i.tldr: CIMSleepNet combines calibrated missing-modality representations with temporal attention to improve sleep staging when physiological signals are incomplete.

paragraphs: A backdoor attack on reinforcement learning aims to make an agent behave normally until it encounters a predetermined trigger, then take an attacker-chosen action. The attack is introduced during training but activated during inference. This paper studies the theoretical reach of such attacks and develops SleeperNets within a newly proposed threat model.

The authors prove limitations in earlier approaches that prevent them from generalizing across domains and Markov decision processes. Their framework links the attacker's objective to the search for an optimal policy, producing an attack-success guarantee in the limit. SleeperNets draws on this analysis and uses dynamic reward poisoning as its attack mechanism.

Experiments span six environments across multiple domains. The attack achieves substantially higher success than existing methods while preserving benign episodic return, meaning normal task performance remains intact in the reported evaluations. The theoretical guarantee is asymptotic, while the experiments provide separate evidence of practical effectiveness. Together, these results show how ordinary performance can coexist with a learned trigger-dependent vulnerability.
neurips-2024-sleepernets-universal-backd.tldr: SleeperNets strengthens trigger-based attacks on reinforcement learning, with an asymptotic success guarantee and improved empirical success while preserving normal returns.

paragraphs: Reconstructing a three-dimensional object from images requires knowing the camera poses, while estimating those poses depends on understanding the object's geometry. With only a few views, this mutual dependence becomes difficult: the images may leave parts of the shape uncertain, and large pose errors can further damage the reconstruction. SparseAGS addresses these coupled problems together.

The method extends analysis by synthesis, which seeks a scene and camera configuration that explain observed pixels. It combines photometric objectives with generative priors based on novel-view synthesis, adding guidance beyond the sparse observations. It also explicitly identifies problematic pose estimates and combines discrete search with continuous optimization to correct these outliers.

The authors evaluate SparseAGS on real and synthetic datasets, starting from several off-the-shelf pose estimators. It significantly improves those systems' pose accuracy and produces reconstructions that outperform current multi-view reconstruction baselines. The findings support using generative guidance for incomplete visual evidence alongside a separate strategy for correcting pose errors that ordinary refinement may struggle to fix.
neurips-2024-sparse-view-pose-estimation.tldr: SparseAGS combines generative view priors with explicit pose-outlier correction to improve camera estimates and 3D reconstruction from sparse images.

paragraphs: Understanding a form requires organizing its text into a document structure, beyond recognizing isolated entities and nearby relationships. The paper argues that existing FUNSD and XFUND annotations emphasize local, entity-level information and therefore miss important hierarchy. SRFUND extends those datasets with annotations designed to evaluate structure across multiple levels of detail.

The benchmark includes five tasks: merging words into text lines, merging lines into entities, classifying entities, locating item tables, and reconstructing the full document hierarchy from entities. The authors supplement missing annotations and add detailed regions for tables containing multiple items. They also introduce global hierarchical dependencies for relation prediction, extending evaluation beyond local key-value associations.

SRFUND covers eight languages: English, Chinese, Japanese, German, French, Spanish, Italian, and Portuguese. Experiments reveal challenges involving diverse layouts and global document organization. The benchmark's contribution is to make these aspects directly testable, linking small-scale text grouping with full-document structure and providing a multilingual basis for studying how those levels interact in form understanding.
neurips-2024-srfund-a-multi-granularity-.tldr: SRFUND extends multilingual form datasets with five tasks that connect word grouping, entities, tables, and full-document hierarchies.

paragraphs: Stochastic optimal control seeks ways to guide systems whose behavior includes randomness. Stochastic Optimal Control Matching, or SOCM, approaches this through a learning objective inspired by conditional score matching in diffusion models. It learns a control function by solving a least-squares problem that fits a matching vector field.

The training objective is closely related to cross-entropy and is optimized over two sets of quantities: the control function and a family of reparameterization matrices appearing in the matching field. Optimizing those matrices aims to reduce the field's variance. The underlying mechanism is a path-wise reparameterization trick, which supplies the basis for this adjustable matching formulation.

In experiments, SOCM obtains lower error than all existing Iterative Diffusion Optimization techniques on three of four control problems, with improvements reaching an order of magnitude in some cases. That result supports its effectiveness while retaining the stated variation across problems. The authors also suggest that the path-wise reparameterization technique may be useful independently of this particular control algorithm.
neurips-2024-stochastic-optimal-control-.tldr: SOCM learns stochastic controls through vector-field matching and variance reduction, achieving lower error on three of four evaluated control problems.

paragraphs: A language model may encounter a fact during training yet fail to retrieve it when the question presents the relationship in a different order. This paper reframes that reversal problem as a factorization problem: learning one ordering of conditional predictions does not reliably teach the same joint information under another ordering.

The authors introduce WikiReversal, a testbed built from Wikipedia knowledge graphs that resembles fine-tuning pretrained models on specialized knowledge. Controlled experiments become progressively more realistic and include non-reciprocal relations. The findings identify next-token prediction as an inherent obstacle to reliable retrieval and show that scaling, reversed tokens, and naive bidirectional-attention training do not resolve the problem.

The paper argues that specialized fine-tuning can consequently yield mixed downstream results unless the model has already encountered the appropriate token sequence. Across five tasks, objectives that are agnostic to factorization significantly mitigate the reversal curse. Those results suggest a promising objective-level change, with potential benefits for knowledge storage and planning rather than an established complete solution to either.
neurips-2024-the-factorization-curse-whi.tldr: The paper links retrieval failures to prediction factorization and finds that factorization-agnostic objectives substantially mitigate the reversal curse.

paragraphs: Multimodal language models can succeed at many visual tasks while still struggling to understand webpage screenshots and produce the corresponding HTML. Web2Code addresses this gap with both training data and an evaluation framework. Its focus includes interpreting webpage content as well as translating a rendered page image into code.

The dataset is constructed using pretrained language models to enrich existing webpage-to-code data and generate diverse new webpages. These pages are rendered into images, creating examples whose inputs contain a webpage image and instructions and whose responses contain HTML. The data also includes natural-language questions and answers about webpage content, broadening the understanding required beyond code production alone.

The evaluation framework tests webpage understanding and image-to-HTML generation. Experiments show benefits from the dataset on these tasks and in the general visual domain. The contribution therefore combines specialized instruction-tuning material with a way to assess the resulting capabilities, supporting research toward multimodal systems for web content generation and task automation.
neurips-2024-web2code-a-large-scale-webp.tldr: Web2Code combines webpage screenshots, HTML, and content questions with an evaluation framework to improve and measure multimodal webpage capabilities.

paragraphs: Fluent language generation does not by itself establish that a model understands tricky or misleading text. FLUB, the FaLlacy Understanding Benchmark, examines this gap using material collected from the real internet. It focuses on texts involving trickiness, humor, and misleading language that the authors characterize as easy for humans to understand but difficult for models.

The benchmark organizes evaluation into three tasks with increasing difficulty. This gives the study a progression of challenges for assessing fallacy understanding, rather than treating the capability as a single undifferentiated outcome. Its use of naturally occurring internet material connects the evaluation to the kinds of confusing language that models may encounter in practice.

The authors test multiple representative advanced language models and find that FLUB remains challenging. Their experiments and detailed analyses motivate further work on this aspect of reasoning and understanding. The main contribution is a focused evaluation resource, accompanied by released data and code, that makes performance on these difficult texts available for systematic study.
neurips-2024-when-llms-meet-cunning-text.tldr: FLUB uses tricky, humorous, and misleading internet texts to expose difficulties in language models' fallacy understanding across three increasingly difficult tasks.
